statement: For each pinned full-length input and each of the four Cas types the app offers, POST /crispr/design reports a total_candidates equal to the number of sites an independent both-strand regex scan of the same raw sequence finds under that nuclease's PAM grammar — the plus strand scanned directly and the minus strand scanned on Biopython's reverse complement, overlapping sites counted individually. The count is over the WHOLE input; no window of the molecule may be silently excluded.

parameters.guide_length: each nuclease's canonical length, the caller passing none: SpCas9 20, SpCas9-HF1 20, AsCas12a 23, LwaCas13a 22

grammar.LwaCas13a: every 22 nt window of the given sense strand, no PAM, no second strand

statement: For every guide the app returns, on either strand and for every Cas type, the reported `sequence` equals the protospacer re-extracted from the raw input BY INDEX at the reported `position`: target[position : position+L] on the plus strand, and Biopython's reverse complement of that same slice on the minus strand. `position` is the leftmost plus-strand index of the protospacer footprint on both strands.

parameters.scope: every guide of every (input, cas_type) pair with max_guides=50

statement: The returned `sequence` is the protospacer and excludes the PAM. Its length equals the guide length in force, and no base of the PAM lies inside the half-open footprint [position, position+L): for a 3'-PAM nuclease the PAM occupies [position+L, position+L+3) on the guide's own strand, for a 5'-PAM nuclease it occupies the four bases immediately 5' of the footprint. This is the invariant #53 broke by letting the PAM's N be captured as the guide's last base.

parameters.check: the PAM slice and the guide slice must be disjoint, and sequence must not contain the PAM bases at either end by construction

statement: The PAM re-extracted from the raw input by index obeys the grammar the app itself reports for that Cas type. SpCas9 and SpCas9-HF1: the three bases 3' of the protospacer match N-G-G (byte-pinned: CRISPOR's PAM table). AsCas12a: the four bases 5' of the protospacer match T-T-T-(A|C|G). LwaCas13a: `pam` is the literal "none", every returned guide is on the given sense strand, and every window is a candidate. UNVERIFIED IN PART: the primary sources for the 5' placement of the Cas12a PAM (Zetsche 2015, PMID 26422227 — "the PAM for FnCpf1 is located upstream of the 5' end of the displaced strand of the protospacer and has the sequence 5'-TTN") and for LwaCas13a having no PFS (Abudayyeh 2017, PMID 28976959 — "no significant PFS motif for LwaCas13a") are PMC author manuscripts released for text mining and fair use only, so they are cited and not vendored; their bytes are not pinned. The app's TTTV is also a narrowing of the literature's TTTN, a design convention rather than a claim about what the nuclease cuts, so the app is held to its own TTTV claim and not to TTTN.

statement: Minus-strand indices map correctly under reverse complement. A guide the app reports at (position p, strand '-') with length L must satisfy: 0 <= p and p+L <= len(target); reverse_complement(target[p:p+L]) equals the reported sequence; and the guide's PAM lies on the far side of the footprint from where a plus-strand guide's would — target[p-3:p] reverse-complemented for an NGG nuclease, target[p+L:p+L+4] reverse-complemented for a TTTV nuclease — so the whole site, PAM included, fits inside the molecule. This is the invariant #64.2 broke by not scanning the minus strand for Cas12a at all.

parameters.bounds: a minus-strand NGG site cannot be reported at p < 3; a minus-strand TTTV site cannot be reported at p > len(target)-L-4

statement: The app names its on-target score after Doench et al. 2014 Rule Set 1 (backend/routers/crispr.py `_doench_rule_set1_score`) and surfaces it to the user as the "On-target" column of the CRISPR panel. A score carrying that name must reproduce the pinned Rule Set 1 definition: intercept 0.59763615, the 70 singleton and dinucleotide weights of `doenchParams`, the GC term abs(10-gcCount) times -0.2026259 (gcCount<=10) or -0.1665878 (gcCount>10), and the logistic 1/(1+exp(-score)), evaluated on the 30mer the model is defined on — 4 nt of 5' context, the 20 nt protospacer, the 3 nt PAM, 3 nt of 3' context. Two consequences are pinned as the failure criteria, so the requirement does not turn on floating-point equality alone: (a) Rule Set 1 depends on the PAM and both flanks, so any score computed from the 20 nt protospacer alone cannot be it; (b) over the 326 SpCas9 sites of full-length pUC19 the app's ordering must agree with Rule Set 1's well enough for max_guides to select the same guides — Spearman rho >= 0.8 and at least 5 of the pinned top 10 shared.

parameters.rs1_30mer: 4 nt 5' context + 20 nt protospacer + 3 nt PAM + 3 nt 3' context

statement: One field, one scale. `on_target_score` is a single field of a single GuideRNA model, coloured by one set of thresholds in the GUI (>=0.6 green, >=0.4 amber, else red) and exported under one TSV column. For any guide the app returns from /crispr/design, the number in that field must equal what the app's own /crispr/score_guide returns for the same sequence. A design call that scores AsCas12a and LwaCas13a guides with a different function from the one /crispr/score_guide uses puts two incomparable scales in one column.

parameters.gui_reference: gui/panels/crispr_panel.py — the On-target column and its row colouring

statement: `max_guides` must select among the candidates, not collapse onto one locus. When the app searches a full-length input and reports thousands of candidates but shows the user only max_guides of them, the shown set must contain at least two mutually non-overlapping sites — otherwise the panel reports 'N guides shown (of M candidates)' while in fact offering one target window in max_guides shifted copies. Pinned as the sharpest case: LwaCas13a on the 24,544 bp COL1A1 record searches 24,523 windows.

parameters.overlap_definition: two guides overlap when abs(pos_a - pos_b) < guide_length

statement: `specificity_score` is presented to the user as an MIT score — the CRISPR panel's off-target checkbox reads 'Scan the target sequence for near-match sites and score guide specificity (MIT)' — and backend/crispr_offtarget.py cites Hsu et al. 2013 and carries that paper's 20 position-specific weights. The defining property of that score is position dependence: a mismatch in the PAM-proximal seed (protospacer position 20, weight 0.583) is far more damaging to an off-target's viability than a PAM-distal one (position 1, weight 0.000). The app's specificity_score must therefore differ between two references that place a guide's single 1-mismatch off-target at those two positions. Pinned from the transcribed definition: hit score 41.7 and Sguide 70.6 for the position-20 mismatch, hit score 100.0 and Sguide 50.0 for the position-1 mismatch.

parameters.carrier: TTTTTT + <20 nt protospacer> + AGG + TTTTTT — one NGG site per reference, flanks that form no second site
parameters.weights_index: index 0 is protospacer position 1 (PAM-distal 5'); index 19 is position 20 (PAM-proximal seed)

statement: SpCas9-HF1 is offered as a distinct nuclease in the CRISPR panel's Cas-type list and described there as 'NGG PAM · high fidelity · fewer off-targets'. Selecting it must therefore change something the user can see: for the same target with off-target checking on, the SpCas9-HF1 response must not be field-for-field identical to the SpCas9 response. Either the specificity model differs, or the option is a label over the same computation and the description is false.

parameters.gui_reference: gui/panels/crispr_panel.py CAS_INFO['SpCas9-HF1'] == 'NGG PAM · high fidelity · fewer off-targets'
parameters.compared_fields: the full GuideRNA model dump of every returned guide, plus total_candidates

statement: The two CRISPR endpoints must agree on what is not a sequence. /crispr/design refuses a target containing any character outside ACGTN with HTTP 400 'Target sequence must be DNA (ACGTN only)'. /crispr/score_guide takes a guide of the same alphabet and must refuse the same way, rather than returning HTTP 200 with a GC percentage computed over the non-nucleotide characters and a categorical 'Good'/'Fair'/'Poor' recommendation. Same family as #87: one input, one verdict, across both endpoints of a capability.

parameters.expected: HTTP 4xx from /crispr/score_guide for a guide of legal length containing a non-ACGTN character

statement: Origin-spanning sites on a circular molecule. Three of the four pinned inputs are circular (pUC19 a plasmid, NC_001699.1 and AF071878.1 complete circular genomes) and the app's own sequence model carries is_circular, which the restriction capability already honours. A guide site that runs through the origin of a circular molecule is a real site; designing against a plasmid must either find those sites or the capability must be reachable with the circularity the app already knows about. Pinned: the exact candidate counts the same grammar yields on the circle versus on the cut-open linear string.

parameters.circular_scan: every start index on the circle matched against the doubled sequence, each site counted once
parameters.note: AF071878.1 AsCas12a is 62 either way — its origin junction happens to carry no TTTV site, which is why three molecules are pinned and not one
